source_ref: Milavic B, Padulo J, Grgantov Z, Milic M, Mannarini S, Manzoni GM, Ardigo LP, Rossi A (2019). PLOS ONE 14(8):e0220930, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0220930 (CC BY 4.0) -- Table 1 (t001) for the 18 item wordings and the response anchors; S1 Dataset (.s001 .xlsx) for the item codes.
note: CLEAN PASS WITH TWO CAVEATS. (1) ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE: the PSIS-Y-SF was administered in Croatian (Milavic et al. 2019 describe translating the PSIS-Y into Croatian and pre-testing it on 30 young volleyball players). The Croatian wording is NOT recoverable from the deposit or the paper's supplements: the article ships exactly one supporting file (S1 Dataset, the .xlsx the IRW script reads), whose 28 headers are bare codes -- ID, Sex, Age, Category, Complete_Category, Train_Hours_Weekly, Train_Start_Age, Years_of_Training, National_TeamPlayer, PSIS-Y-SF_01..18 and one empty Excel-overflow column literally headed '#########' -- with zero item text at any level and no Croatian anywhere in the file. So the fallback applies: English in the base fields, _translated columns empty, text_source=translated_substitute, language=Croatian. The English shipped is this study's own Table 1 (translation_source=study_supplied), which is the PSIS-Y lineage wording in English. (2) RESPONSE ANCHORS: the paper contradicts itself. Its Methods say 'Items were scaled on five-point Likert scale ranging from 1 (= almost never) to 5 (= almost always)', while the Table 1 footnote -- the table describing these very 18 items, and the source of the %Min/%Max used to verify the mapping -- says '%Min = percentage of subjects, who choose the first category of response (1 = strongly disagree); %Max = percentage of subjects who choose the last category of response (5 = strongly agree)'. The Table 1 footnote is shipped, on two grounds: it is the statement attached to these 18 items rather than a general Methods sentence, and the PSIS-R5 parent instrument is an agreement scale (Rihtars et al. 2025, PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0325225: 'ranging from 1 (completely disagree) to 5 (completely agree)'). Both readings run negative-to-positive, so resp ordering and the reverse-keyed items are unaffected either way -- only the anchor labels are in doubt. Scale points 2, 3 and 4 are unlabelled in the source and ship blank rather than padded with their own numbers. TRANSCRIPTION: literal from the Table 1 image (the PLOS table is an image; text routes return nothing for it), fetched as journals.plos.org/plosone/article/figure/image?size=large&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0220930.t001. The paper's '(R)' reverse-scoring markers are annotation, not wording, and were stripped from the 6 items carrying them (7, 8, 9, 16, 17, 18); printed typography (curly quotes around 'rehearse' and 'see', en dashes in items 11 and 14, the typographic apostrophe in item 15) is kept as printed. The live data are RAW, not reverse-scored: all 18 live per-item means/SDs reproduce Table 1 exactly, including the six (R) items. No instructions text is published anywhere in the paper or the deposit, so instructions is blank. RIGHTS: no restriction locatable to quote. The PSIS-Y-SF wording comes from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article; the upstream PSIS / PSIS-5R / PSIS-Y (Mahoney, Gabriel & Perkins) has no rights-holder distribution page, no fee, no permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term that could be found and quoted. Ships under silence-is-permission, which is weaker than an express grant; no register row was written, per the rule that a round may write 'block' but never 'ship'.
public_note: Item wording for this table is English while the instrument was administered in Croatian: the study's data deposit and its single supplementary file carry no Croatian text, so the English printed in the paper's Table 1 is shipped in its place, and the anchors in option_text (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree) are taken from that table's footnote even though the same paper's Methods section instead describes the scale as running from 1 = almost never to 5 = almost always

note: CLEAN PASS WITH CAVEATS (batch_306). Item set 30/30 and resp set 21/21 (0-100 by 5s) match irw_table_sets() exactly; irw-validate clean. mapping_basis=data_labels: data/risticdedic_2025_dhq.py derives `item` by stripping the '_currentstate' suffix from the source .sav column name, so the IRW code IS the source column name and the .sav's own variable labels carry each statement -- a name-preserving rename, exempt from Step 5b. The Zenodo codebook (10.5281/zenodo.15349256) independently prints a QUESTION FULL TEXT block per variable NAME, so the tie is a label match at two levels, not an order inference. CAVEAT 1 (SPSS typo corrected): development3_currentstate's variable label reads '...is developed tho address the needs...'. Both the administered questionnaire (10.5281/zenodo.13767190, A.3) and the codebook's QUESTION FULL TEXT for that same variable read 'to address', as does development3_importance's own label; 'tho' is a typo in two of the three facet labels and was corrected. 25 of the other 29 item_text strings reproduce their .sav label character for character after stripping the ' - CURRENT STATE' facet suffix and non-breaking spaces. CAVEAT 2 (terse labels expanded): the four organisational-value items (participation, acctrans, EDI, ecosocresp) carry .sav labels that are bare value names ('Participation', 'Accountability and transparency', ...). The labels were used for the MAPPING and the questionnaire's own definition paragraph for the WORDS -- e.g. participation ships 'Participation refers to the active involvement of students, staff...'. The questionnaire renders the value name as a heading directly above a lowercase-opening definition, so the concatenation is the sentence respondents read, not an IRW gloss. CAVEAT 3 (which prompt wording): the administered questionnaire's per-item CURRENT STATE prompt is 'To what extent is this practice currently present in educational programmes of your school?', identical for all 30 items including the four values. The codebook prints a shortened variant ('...currently present in your school?', and 'this value' for the four values). The administered PDF wording ships, in `instructions`, because it does not vary by section. CAVEAT 4 (endpoints only): the slider is 0-100 and only its endpoints are labelled, and only in the instructions ('on a scale from 0% (not at all) to 100% (very much)'). resp=0 gets 'not at all', resp=100 gets 'very much', and the other 19 levels get a blank option_text rather than being padded with their own number. CAVEAT 5 (multi-language): 10 administered languages across 9 countries (Croatian 196, Dutch 170, Finnish 92, German 90, English 87, Catalan 73, Slovenian 59, French 33, Greek 18, Spanish 16 schools). `language` lists all ten by sample share per the szameitat_2015 precedent. The base fields hold the English MASTER version, which is one of the ten administered forms (the 87 Irish schools) and the version the other nine were translated from; the _translated columns are therefore omitted, not left empty. All ten versions are in the same Zenodo PDF if a later pass wants them. CAVEAT 6 (instrument name): the dataset/codebook records call it the 'Democratic Health Questionnaire'; the instrument deliverable itself is titled 'Democracy Health Questionnaire (DHQ) for Schools'. The dataset spelling ships, matching the IRW table name. RIGHTS: no block. The DHQ is the depositing authors' own instrument (Jokic, Matic Bojic, Ristic Dedic, Baketa / Institute for Social Research Zagreb), published by them on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at 10.5281/zenodo.13767190 (Zenodo API metadata.license.id = 'cc-by-4.0'), and the codebook at 10.5281/zenodo.15349256 is CC BY 4.0 too. No fee, no non-commercial, no no-derivatives and no redistribution bar appears on either record or in the PDFs; the only restriction-shaped text is the standard Horizon Europe disclaimer that views expressed are the authors' own, which disclaims responsibility rather than reserving a right. No upstream originator: the instrument was built for this project, not adapted from a third party's scale. Nothing added to instrument_rights_register.csv (a round may not write a `ship` row). SCOPE: the sibling tables risticdedic_2025_dhq_expectation and _importance were read but NOT built -- they remain pending. They share this item pool; their stems and per-item prompts differ ('How important do you consider this practice?' / 'To what extent do you expect this practice will be present ... in 5 years?'), so their instructions and section framing are NOT reusable from this file verbatim.
public_note: The DHQ was administered in ten languages across nine EU countries (Croatian, Dutch, Finnish, German, English, Catalan, Slovenian, French, Greek and Spanish); the item text shipped here is the English master version, which 87 of the 834 schools answered directly and from which the other nine versions were translated. All ten language versions are published by the authors at doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13767190. The 0-100 slider is labelled only at its endpoints, so option_text is populated for resp=0 and resp=100 only.

public_note: Item codes ARE the source data's own QuestionID values: data/trivia_fastrich_2017.py renames QuestionID -> item with no renumbering and no positional assignment, so the tie between code and question wording is made row by row inside the source file rather than inferred. Stronger still, the same script carries Question -> cov_question and corrAnswer -> cov_corranswer into the IRW table itself, so the mapping is checkable against the live data without reference to any external document; verify_trivia_fastrich_2017.R does exactly that (244/244 shipped wordings appear under their own item code, 0 under any other). item_text is the Question string verbatim and correct_response the corrAnswer string verbatim; no normalisation of either. FIVE item codes (135, 167, 224, 234, 267) carry TWO administered wordings, because the study corrected them part way through data collection -- 'poisonous'->'venomous' (135, 234), 'county'->'country' (167), 'gas marks'->'gas masks' (224), and a mojibake 'Hippolyte M?EEge-Mouri?EEs' repaired to 'Hippolyte Mege-Mouries' (267). The early wording ran 2015-02-13 to 2015-02-17 and the corrected wording from 2015-02-22 onward, so the later, corrected string is what ships for each; see the public_note. INSTRUCTIONS ARE BLANK by choice: neither the deposit nor the paper prints verbatim instruction text for the recall task, only a procedural description ('participants were presented with the same set of questions ... and were asked to recall the answer to the question within 10-12 seconds'), and paraphrasing that into an instructions field would misrepresent it as wording respondents read. option_text is the scoring of the response rather than a printed option: resp is Memory.sACC, documented as 'Accuracy of participants guess in the second session (note: during the first session it was always incorrect)', so 0='Incorrect' and 1='Correct'; the participants' own free-text answers live in cov_response. RIGHTS: the instrument is the authors' own pool of 303 trivia questions assembled from Kang et al. (2009), Nelson & Narens (1980), Gruber et al. (2014) and online sources; no fee, no-redistribution, non-commercial or permission-required clause could be located for it or for the OSF deposit (the node declares no licence at all -- node_license null on api.osf.io/v2/nodes/kjahf), so silence-is-permission applies and no rights-register row was written. Noted for completeness: the wording is already published inside the IRW response table as cov_question, so withholding it here would not reach it (irw#2101).
